schema_note: Milestone 10C Phase 2 -- independently-authored heading-classification truth, kept deliberately SEPARATE from any parser or candidate-classifier output. Evaluation data only, never imported by src/gitscore. Not wired to any production code path.
annotation_honesty_note: Per this project's standing precedent (M9B's blind-annotation discipline; M10A's own retraction of a false blind-annotation claim), stated honestly: these controls were authored by reasoning about each fragment's real-world meaning on a fresh read -- drawing on the already-published M10A root-cause findings and the real SOTI/Manulife wording for traceability -- and were NOT derived by running any candidate classifier first and reverse-engineering a label from its output. No candidate classifier implementation existed yet when this file was written. This is closer to M9B's discipline than M10A's own corpus (which explicitly retracted a blind-annotation claim), but it is not independently enforced by a structural test the way M9B's is, so no stronger guarantee is claimed than 'authored before any classifier code, not checked against one afterward.' Several entries are deliberately marked ambiguous=true with documented reasoning rather than forced to one answer -- an honest annotation records real disagreement potential instead of hiding it.

Already recognized today -- must not regress.

Milestone-mandated example. Annotated REQUIRED because this heading idiom overwhelmingly introduces a required-skills list in real postings, but it carries NO required-family root word at all (no 'requir*'/'qualif*'/'must have') -- a root-word classifier has no principled way to recognize it without either a literal exact-phrase entry or a much broader (and riskier) 'skills' root. Marked ambiguous to record this honestly rather than claim a clean win for any design.

U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE between the two words instead of an ASCII space -- a common copy/paste-from-web artifact. A classifier using a plain '\s' regex class already matches NBSP (it's in Python's Unicode \s set), but an exact-match table doing naive ASCII lowering/compare could still diverge if any step assumes ASCII-only whitespace folding -- must be measured, not assumed.

Milestone-mandated example and a genuine compound heading -- it legitimately introduces a section with BOTH qualification bullets and duty bullets, which no single section-kind tag can represent faithfully. Annotated UNKNOWN/ambiguous deliberately: a design that confidently picks either REQUIRED or RESPONSIBILITY alone is making an unsupported claim about content it has not actually seen yet. This is a design-relevant finding, not just a hard test case -- see Phase 6.

Explicit milestone-listed collision. Annotated RESPONSIBILITY on the reading that 'Required' here modifies the MANDATORINESS of the duties listed (these are core, non-optional duties), not an applicant qualification -- but this is a judgment call, not an obviously correct one; UNKNOWN is also defensible. A classifier confidently returning REQUIRED is making the less-defensible of the two readings.

A second compound-heading variant, structurally identical in kind to 016 (mixes a qualifications root and a responsibilities root), included to confirm a classifier's compound-heading handling is a general policy, not a one-off special case for 016's exact wording.

Explicit milestone collision control ('Preferred Skills' vs REQUIRED) -- must resolve to PREFERRED despite containing no REQUIRED-family word; a classifier that over-matches on a bare 'skills' root would risk this.

Already recognized today. The central collision this milestone cares most about: contains the REQUIRED-family root 'qualif*' AND the PREFERRED-family root 'preferr*' in the same phrase -- any root-word design MUST special-case this exact interaction or it mis-fires as REQUIRED.

Explicit milestone collision control. This is a REQUIREMENT CLAIM with an inline example list, never a section boundary, even though it contains a colon -- the colon is NOT at the end of the line (content follows it on the same line). A detector that treats 'contains a colon anywhere' as heading-shaped would wrongly flag this; today's own M10B rule happens to avoid it only because M10B's trigger specifically requires the line to itself END in a colon.

Explicit milestone collision control. Structurally ambiguous ON PURPOSE: this line DOES end in a bare colon with nothing following, satisfying M10B's existing non-bulleted heading-reset trigger shape exactly -- yet it is a list lead-in, not a real section heading, whenever it appears inside an already-open recognized section (mirrors the already-fixed bulleted case, 'm10b-12', but WITHOUT a bullet marker, which M10B's fix does not cover). Annotated is_heading=false because its most common real-world role is a list lead-in; flagged ambiguous because, read with zero surrounding context (as a bare, isolated line), 'ends in a colon, no family root, short' is genuinely indistinguishable from a true UNKNOWN heading using only this single line -- disambiguating it correctly requires knowing it is a CONTINUATION of an already-open section, which is a document-level fact no single-line classifier alone can resolve.
The bulleted sibling of 058, already correctly fixed by M10B's bullet-exemption amendment ('m10b-12' control) -- included here as a baseline regression control any M10C design must not break.

A second bare (unbulleted), colon-terminated list lead-in, same shape class as 058 with different wording -- confirms the false-positive risk is about the STRUCTURAL SHAPE (short, colon-terminated, technical-lead-in phrase), not about one exact sentence.

Shortest, most extreme version of the bare-colon list-lead-in shape -- two words before the colon, no family root word visible at all. The minimal case any 'ends in colon => heading-shaped' rule must handle without flagging it.

A single generic word plus colon -- genuinely ambiguous between a true (if unhelpfully generic) section heading and a mid-sentence list lead-in. Annotated UNKNOWN/ambiguous rather than forced to REQUIRED, since nothing about the bare word 'Skills' alone signals REQUIRED over PREFERRED or a list lead-in with equal confidence.

controls.text: Required qualifications are reviewed by our hiring team before any interview is scheduled.
controls.rationale: Full sentence (ends in '.', multiple clauses, a verb) that happens to contain the exact two-word phrase 'Required qualifications' -- must NOT be classified as a REQUIRED heading. Tests whether a heading-detection stage genuinely checks sentence SHAPE (length, terminal punctuation) rather than only phrase content.

controls.text: We believe the preferred approach to growth is continuous learning.
controls.rationale: Ordinary sentence incidentally containing both 'preferred' and 'learning' root words -- a pure root-word scan with no sentence-shape gate would risk misfiring here. Must be excluded as not-a-heading entirely.

controls.text: Candidates must demonstrate strong responsibility and ownership in their daily work.
controls.rationale: Ordinary sentence containing the 'respons*' root as a personal-trait noun ('responsibility and ownership'), not as a section heading about job duties -- a different sense of the same root entirely.

controls.text: This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to learn about distributed systems.
controls.rationale: Ordinary marketing-prose sentence containing both 'opportunity' and 'learn' -- the exact two words the LEARNING family's roots key on -- but is plainly a sentence (subject, verb, terminal period), not a heading.

Leading tab character before an otherwise-already-recognized phrase -- a plausible artifact of some ATS exports. Leading/trailing whitespace trimming (already present in today's `_line_content_span`) should already handle this; included to confirm that holds for a tab specifically, not only ASCII spaces.

Trailing U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE -- invisible in rendered text but present in the raw string, a realistic copy/paste-from-web artifact. Python's default '\s'/`.strip()` do NOT treat U+200B as whitespace, so naive trimming leaves it attached to the phrase, breaking an exact-match lookup silently (the line looks identical to a human, and the mismatch has no visible symptom) -- this is deliberately included as a trap for any design that assumes `.strip()`/`.lower()` alone is sufficient Unicode normalization.

A genuinely generic catch-all heading with no reliable family signal at all -- correctly annotated UNKNOWN rather than forced into any of the five named families. A design that confidently assigns this to one risks fabricating certainty it has no basis for.

Another genuinely vague catch-all heading idiom, sometimes used for logistics/perks (NON_QUALIFICATION-leaning) and sometimes for a true grab-bag -- annotated UNKNOWN as the more conservative choice, NON_QUALIFICATION flagged as also acceptable.
Colon-terminated variant of the already-recognized bare 'Qualifications' -- baseline regression control.
Colon-terminated variant of 048 -- baseline regression control.

Already recognized today -- baseline positive control, and a second confirmation (alongside 041/045-047) that the generic 'about <noun phrase>' structural pattern covers both the templated phrase and a real company name.
All-lowercase, colon-terminated variant of an already-recognized phrase -- baseline case-folding regression control.

A second inline-colon-list requirement claim (structurally identical to 057's class, different lead-in phrase and a fictional-company framing) -- confirms the false-positive risk generalizes beyond the one milestone-given wording.

A fourth fictional company, embedded mid-phrase (not as a leading 'About <X>' pattern) inside an otherwise LEARNING-family heading -- confirms a company name appearing somewhere in a heading must never, by itself, suppress or override an otherwise-correct family match.
